text:
maria-ops: Heads-up — thinking about moving most low-priority batch training and evals to nightly off-peak spot-only pools. Want to sync on interruption handling and interactive fallbacks.
jonathan: +1. Can we quantify expected savings? Also worried about cross-region constraints — APAC spot supply is flaky.
cheng: We ran a small experiment: 72h off-peak batch using preemptible-only in us-west1 saved ~62% vs on-demand but had ~18% retry rate due to interruptions.
priyanka: How are we handling live interactive jobs? Latency-sensitive inference can't be on preemptible. Suggest mixed-capacity pool per queue: interactive pinned to on-demand, batch to spot-first.
maria-ops: Proposed policy: 80% of batch queue capacity = spot-preferred with 2-tier fallback: within-pool fallback to cheaper persistent-gpu variants, then to on-demand if total capacity < threshold.
cheng: Example autoscaler config I'm testing:
```
queues.batch: {
  capacity_target: 100,
  spot_preference: true,
  fallback_order: ["g4dn-spot","a100-persistent","a100-on-demand"],
  eviction_policy: "graceful-drain-5m"
}
```
jonathan: Graceful drain + KV cache snapshotting is crucial for generation workloads — how do we snapshot large KV caches quickly?
priyanka: We can push cache checkpoints every 2 minutes for long runs; for short interactive sessions we shouldn't rely on spot. Also set queue priority weight: interactive 100, batch 10.
infra-bot: Alert: preemptible pool in us-east1 experienced 12% interruption spike at 23:10 UTC — automatic rescale triggered.
cheng: That spike correlates with a major maintenance event in provider — we should add region-aware routing policy: prefer us-west1/us-central for night jobs, avoid APAC.
maria-ops: Ops checklist for rollout:
- set queue priorities
- implement fallback_order
- add monitoring alert for interrupt rate > 5%
- add cost baseline metric
Anyone willing to own rollout next week?
jonathan: I'll take rollout and run canary in 3 clusters (dev, staging, prod-lite).
priyanka: I'll produce a quick playbook for developer UX when jobs get preempted — notify owners, rerun hints, resource suggestions.
maria-ops: Nice. Also add a short Slack notify pattern: `@{owner} your job <id> was preempted — auto-retry scheduled` with link to rerun button.
cheng: One more ask — add throttling for on-demand promotions during surge to avoid cost spike: budget cap + rate limiter.
maria-ops: Agreed. We'll aim for 50% of expected cost savings preserved by capping on-demand fallback to X GPUs/hour.
